findings.reason: an implementer following the four-site census and the "each of the four sites calls it" test will consolidate four sites and leave a path-based sibling of the same resolution in `routing.py`, so §16 ships claiming one owner while a fifth spelling survives and the second test cannot detect it.
findings.text: §16 enumerates exactly four sites that resolve a repository path to its projects and says "Keep one identity-based resolver ... and make all four sites call it", but `resolve_dispatch_authority` in `reckon/crew/routing.py:3302-3333` performs the same resolution — `work_projects = sorted(name for name, docs in mounts.items() if docs.parent.resolve() == work_repo)` — by a resolved-path comparison (worktree-blind, the same defect class as the `shadow_source` and `_project_for_repository` rows) and reads `flight.mounted_project_docs()` directly rather than `mounted_repository_projects()`, so the census's instrument cannot see it; it sits in the very module §16 names as the owner's home, and leaving it unconverted defeats the section's stated goal of one owner.
